content.intro: Learn mocking and external services through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Mocking and External Services matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines mocking and external services as part of testing and code quality. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Mocking external HTTP calls; Mocking email delivery; Isolating payment-provider behavior; Testing retry conditions; Avoiding excessive mocking of internal code. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Mocking external HTTP calls
items.text: Mock only the boundary being isolated, such as an external API client, and assert the important interaction. Add integration tests with local fakes where behavior depends on real framework/database semantics.

items.title: Mocking email delivery
items.text: Mock only the boundary being isolated, such as an external API client, and assert the important interaction. Add integration tests with local fakes where behavior depends on real framework/database semantics.

items.title: Isolating payment-provider behavior
items.text: Treat the browser redirect as untrusted. Verify payment state server-side with the provider, validate amount/currency/order association, verify signed webhooks, and make duplicate events harmless.

items.title: Testing retry conditions
items.text: A good test covers an observable contract and asserts status, output, database changes or access denial. Include invalid and boundary inputs so a regression does not only fail on a happy path.

items.title: Avoiding excessive mocking of internal code
items.text: Mock only the boundary being isolated, such as an external API client, and assert the important interaction. Add integration tests with local fakes where behavior depends on real framework/database semantics.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Mocking and External Services
content_blocks.code:
from django.core.mail import send_mail

send_mail("Notice", "Example message", None, ["learner@example.test"], fail_silently=False)
content_blocks.expected_output: A configured backend handles the send operation and reports failures according to its settings.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Mocking external HTTP calls. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting input or relying only on a happy-path example.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid values, unauthorized requests, or concurrent activity can violate assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and add a negative or boundary test.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating the development sample as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Production hosting, secrets, storage, monitoring and resource limits differ from local use.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the current deployment/security references and document untested areas.
